# Paxton Lumnus

I was born along the Eastern Rivers, in a city called Havens Reach. Tired of the unchanging rhythms of the city, I enlisted with the Spinewardens to serve the Light where it mattered most. I was stationed at The Spine they call Hallowreach when the wards began to fail. Something from beyond the Bonewall was pressing through. We held as long as we could, but it became clear the Spine would fall. 

A long-hidden ritual was offered to anchor the Light directly but with one catch: the ritual required a sacrifice. I volunteered. The breach closed and as was expected, I died. They laid me in the Spine’s mausoleum.

I woke.

As the light of a new dawn burned my eyes, it showed me something it hadn’t before: that the wards themselves were flawed. Without telling anyone, I left for Aurelion seeking the Light’s truth.

# Playbook: Immolator

Reskinned for The Light

# Background

## Dawn Unending (Heart of the Phoenix)

*You sacrificed your entire being, but were returned to life shortly afterward with the Light in your heart. You may have ‘died’ several times since then, but it never seems to take. Each time you come back, something is different.*

**When you Crumble**, replace “Die” with “Die for now, then return to life when everyone next Settles In.”

**Starting Stats**: \+2 CHA, \+1 STR  
**Equipment**: Adventuring Gear (5 Uses)  
**Drive**: Act callously or recklessly about death

# Starting Moves

## Lightbrand (Firebrand)

You can move and manipulate light in a variety of ways \- dimming, flaring, sparking, changing color, creating shapes and images, and more. Your light is **Distinctive**, **Fiery**, and **Near** when you fight with it.

Fiery: this still tracks: burns, sears, causes things to catch fire, like a magnifying glass focusing light  
	  
Additionally, choose two traits for it:  
• **Restrained**: You and nearby allies have \+1 Armor against your light and its effects.   
This is probably the trait/tag I will Burn first most of the time as a representation of the loss of control and the loss of the preservative quality of Light.  
• **Spontaneous**: You can create light rather than manipulate what’s already burning.  
I am an embodiment of the Light, of course I can create it.  
When you Burn a trait, your light loses it until you next Settle In.

## Unleash Radiance (Unleash Flames)

**When you fight using light as a weapon**, roll+CHA.  
On a 10+ you hurt your foe, but choose one.  
On a 7-9 you hurt your foe, but choose two.  
• You cause unintended collateral damage  
• You suffer a condition, perhaps due to overexertion or a foe’s counterattack  
Conditions will likely focus on things like “Blinded” or “Stunned”  
• Choose and Burn one of your light’s traits  
• Your draw unwanted attention from nearby

## Righteous Illumination (From the Ashes)

**When you offer a sacrifice to the Light and illuminate it utterly**, ask the GM one question about your sacrifice or something associated with it (owners, loved ones, history, etc.) and roll+CHA.

On a 10+ you receive a clear and detailed vision that answers your question and related follow-up questions.  
 On a 7–9 you receive a brief or incomplete vision that answers your question vaguely.

The sacrifice may be a physical object or metaphysical ideas, emotions, memories, etc. Once exposed to the Light, it is gone forever. The depth of truth revealed is proportional to the significance of what was given up.

The Light does not lie—but it may show uncomfortable truths without context or mercy.

## Drawn to the Light (Captivate)

**When you share an intimate or revealing moment with someone**, usually with time and  
privacy, roll+CHA.  
On a 10+ you have 2 Charm over them.  
On a 7-9 you have 1 Charm over them.  
They can reduce your Charm over them by 1 by:  
• Giving you something they think you want.  
• Doing something you tell them to do.  
• Fighting to protect you.  
• Favoring you, but only if they don’t already.  
If they’re an NPC, they can’t act out against you while Charmed. If they’re a PC, you also can spend 1 Charm to inspire or distract them, granting them Advantage or Disadvantage on their next roll.

# Ask

Who here knows me from before the Light? (Roderick?)  
Who here am I still trying to enamor or impress? (Castor?)  
Who here is trying to guide or control me? (Garland?)

# Answer

When did the Light inside last get truly out of control?  
What did you sacrifice to gain your Light?   
What foreboding vision did the Light show you? The wards supporting the Spires, that keep the darkness on the other side of the Bonewall at bay, are flawed. Lucifer did not protect Beaconhold indefinitely. He just prolonged its inevitable Ruin.

# Favor

Initially, you Favor the PC who’s been burned by your Light. What caused this? What did they lose?

### 1\. What faction does your hero belong to? Where are they from? 

Paxton is from Haven’s Reach, a stagnant port town on the Solivum where Beaconhold, the Eastern Rivers, and the lake meet. The town sits inside the bones of a much larger Imperium-era city: old foundations too large for modern homes, dead streets that lead nowhere, and ruined walls from a forgotten age. It is a place built around trade, memory, and arrested possibility. 

#### 2\. How would you physically describe your Hero?

Paxton Lumnus is a human man in his early thirties, tall, lean, and weathered, with the posture of a former soldier who still expects inspection. His short dark-blond hair has grown uneven since leaving Hallowreach, with pale gold-white streaks near the temples. He wears smoky leather armor over practical travel clothes; the old Spinewarden marks have been scraped off, but not well enough to hide what he was. His eyes seem normal at first, except for unnaturally bright amber-gold irises patterned like sunrise through smoked glass. He looks less like a saint than a dead soldier whom the dawn refused to release. 

#### 3\. Does your Hero have recurring mannerisms?

When anxious or angry, he rubs one thumb across the center of his chest where the ritual burns are hidden under his armor. He avoids saying “I died” casually; instead he says things like “the first time I fell” or “before the dawn took me back.” When the Light stirs in him, he goes unnervingly still before acting.

#### 4\. What is your Hero’s main motivation?

**Paxton’s main motivation is to uncover the truth of the Light before more people die trusting a flawed protection.** He still believes the Light saved lives, including his own, but he no longer believes its institutions understand what they are holding back. What keeps him going is not revenge or ambition, but the need to know whether Lucifer’s legacy can be repaired — or whether it must be exposed. Beneath that is guilt: he survived the sacrifice, and now he has to make that survival mean something. 

#### 5\. What is your Hero’s greatest strength? Greatest weakness?

**Paxton’s greatest strength is conviction under pressure: when the line breaks, he can still stand there and burn bright enough for others to rally behind.** He is brave, compelling, and willing to pay the cost himself rather than ask it of someone else. His greatest weakness is that he mistakes sacrifice for judgment; because he died once and returned, he is too quick to treat his own survival, pain, and death as expendable. He can become reckless, especially when the Light offers a terrible answer that feels like truth. 

#### 6\. What are your Hero’s most and least favorite things?

**Paxton’s favorite things are dawn over water, hot black tea, and the sound of harbor work beginning before the rest of the city wakes.** He likes practical soldier’s food: dark bread, smoked fish, river onions. He hates enclosed spaces and will sometimes awake in a cold sweat, remembering the mausoleum where he woke.
